# Delegation Risk Checklist: Web API Integration

**Purpose**: Requirements-quality gate for the tasks in `plan.md` where a low-capability model would have to *invent a value* to proceed. These are not the interesting tasks — they are the ones where guessing wrong produces code that typechecks, lints, and silently breaks authentication.
**Created**: 2026-10-02
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [plan.md](../plan.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

**How to read the "Wrong shape" lines.** Each item states the specific wrong answer that satisfies the plan's letter while breaking its intent. A plan task is only delegable if there is no plausible wrong answer left — so an item is unsatisfied whenever the wrong shape is still reachable by a reasonable reader.

**Gate semantics**: `/speckit-implement` reads checkbox state and must not modify markers. All items unchecked blocks implementation.

---

## Requirement Clarity — Single-Valued Decisions

- [x] CHK001 - Is the refresh cookie's `Path` stated as exactly one literal value, identical in spec, plan, contracts, data-model, and quickstart? **Wrong shape**: each document names a different path, so the implementer picks whichever file they opened first. [Consistency, Spec §FR-016 / Plan T01]
- [x] CHK002 - Is the *consequence* of each candidate `Path` documented (which requirement each one breaks), rather than the correct value being asserted only as a mandate? **Wrong shape**: "`Path=/`" with no stated reason — an implementer who believes `/api/auth` is more precise has no way to learn they are wrong. [Clarity, Spec §FR-016]
- [x] CHK003 - Does the plan state the refresh cookie's literal name and its source file, or does it instruct the implementer to locate it? **Wrong shape**: "read the cookie name from the backend" with no value — a model invents `refreshToken`, `refresh_token`, or `session`, and the guard silently never matches. [Clarity, Plan T08]
- [x] CHK004 - Is the proxy guard's decision explicitly specified as a presence check, with the reason it cannot validate the token? **Wrong shape**: the requirement reads "the guard verifies the session", implying cryptographic validation that is impossible for an opaque Redis UUID in middleware. [Clarity, Spec §FR-008]
- [x] CHK005 - Is the outcome specified for a stale cookie that passes the presence check? **Wrong shape**: unspecified — an implementer adds a second network call from middleware to "fix" the gap, adding latency to every navigation. [Completeness, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK006 - Does the session-restore requirement name **one decided** source for the user object after a reload, rather than presenting options for the implementer to choose from? **Wrong shape**: "fetch the user separately or re-fetch the profile" — an undecided fork is precisely where a cheap model improvises. [Clarity, Plan T12 / Spec §FR-019]
- [x] CHK007 - Is it stated that the refresh response carries no user object today, and that no profile endpoint exists, so a decision was required? **Wrong shape**: the requirement assumes a user is available on refresh, leading the implementer to read `data.user` and store `undefined`. [Completeness, Gap, Plan T12]
- [x] CHK008 - Is the "must not loop" requirement quantified as an exact call count per page load? **Wrong shape**: "must not retry in a loop" without a number — a model implementing two attempts would argue it is not a loop. [Measurability, Spec §FR-019]
- [x] CHK009 - Is the required interval between first paint and the restore outcome specified (whether a login screen may flash)? **Wrong shape**: unstated, so a model renders the login redirect before the restore resolves and reintroduces the flash the requirement exists to prevent. [Completeness, Spec §FR-019]
- [x] CHK010 - Is the retry budget stated numerically — method, attempt count, and delays — in one authoritative location? **Wrong shape**: policy prose spread across FR-011 and FR-021 with different numbers. [Measurability, Spec §FR-021]
- [x] CHK011 - Is the prohibition on client-side password rules stated relative to the server's actual rule, rather than as an abstract "match the server"? **Wrong shape**: the model invents a strength meter the backend never enforces, producing a confusing rejection for a password the UI called valid. [Clarity, Spec §FR-025]

## Requirement Consistency — Single Source of Truth

- [x] CHK012 - Are the frontend types that contradict the backend enumerated with the wire-truth for each, so none is silently left in place? **Wrong shape**: "fix the types in `types.ts`" with no list — `ApiResponse.success`, `Role.CUSTOMER_SERVICE`, and `AuthUser.name/department/status` are three separate defects, and a model fixing one believes it finished. [Completeness, Plan T07]
- [x] CHK013 - Is the requirement stated that role display labels never render the raw wire value, with the `CS` mapping specified? **Wrong shape**: the requirement is only "handle CS correctly" — the UI then displays `CS` verbatim. [Clarity, Spec §FR-007 / Plan T07]
- [x] CHK014 - Are the two distinct no-data states (no data source vs failed fetch) each specified with an outcome that differs observably? **Wrong shape**: both render an em-dash, so a failed fetch is indistinguishable from a KPI with no endpoint and offers no retry. [Consistency, Spec §FR-006 / FR-023]
- [x] CHK015 - Is the empty-state requirement specified separately for each surface (KPI cards vs table)? **Wrong shape**: stated once for "the dashboard", leaving the table's behaviour to inference. [Completeness, Spec §FR-023]
- [x] CHK016 - Are the requirements prohibiting JavaScript access to the refresh token stated once, without contradiction, across FR-002, FR-020, and the plan? **Wrong shape**: the requirements restate the prohibition but an adjacent task reintroduces a store field for it. [Consistency, Spec §FR-002 / FR-020]
- [x] CHK017 - Is the changed `setSession` signature specified such that the old three-argument call cannot compile? **Wrong shape**: described as "no longer stores a refresh token" while keeping the parameter — the value is still in memory and still XSS-readable. [Clarity, Plan T06]
- [x] CHK018 - Is it stated that the backend work is already complete, so it is not repeated? **Wrong shape**: a task list that includes "set the refresh cookie" and "enable CORS" — both shipped in `ee32f3b` — inviting a model to rebuild working code. [Completeness, Dependency, Plan §Scope reality check]

## Requirement Completeness — Decisions That Must Already Be Made

- [x] CHK019 - Is the requirement for the users list stated for a `UserDto` that has no `name` field — i.e. which columns exist? **Wrong shape**: columns inherited from the removed mock data include name and status, which render blank because the backend never sends them. [Completeness, Gap, Spec §FR-007]
- [x] CHK020 - Are the route-existence requirements for `forgot-password` and `reset-password` stated, given both pages currently sit outside the App Router and are not routes? **Wrong shape**: the requirement says "wire the pages", implying they are reachable — a model edits the files in place and both URLs still 404. [Completeness, Spec §FR-024 / Plan T13]
- [x] CHK021 - Are non-enumeration requirements stated distinctly for login and for `forgot-password`, including that the confirmation text must be byte-identical? **Wrong shape**: "do not reveal whether the email exists" without specifying identical output, so the two branches differ in wording. [Completeness, Spec §FR-022 / FR-024]
- [x] CHK022 - Is the non-enumeration requirement stated as covering the status code, not only the rendered message? **Wrong shape**: only the UI is constrained, and the API response still distinguishes the cases. [Completeness, Spec §FR-022]
- [x] CHK023 - Are the port requirements unambiguous about which process owns which port? **Wrong shape**: both configured for 3000, so neither starts. [Completeness, Plan T02 / T16]
- [x] CHK024 - Is it specified which API base URL may reach the browser bundle, and the consequence of a `NEXT_PUBLIC_` value? **Wrong shape**: unstated, so the rewrite target is inlined into client-side code and the internal host ships to users. [Completeness, Security, Plan T02]
- [x] CHK025 - Is there an explicit prohibition on adding backend fields or endpoints not present in the contract? **Wrong shape**: unstated, so a model extends `RefreshTokenResponseDto` to carry the user it needs — frontend and backend then disagree about the contract. [Completeness, Plan T12]
- [x] CHK026 - Is the requirement for obtaining the current user profile stated as a known gap, given no `/auth/me` endpoint exists? **Wrong shape**: a model calls `GET /auth/me` because `endpoints.ts` already declares one, and gets a 404. [Completeness, Gap, Plan T12]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK027 - Is each of T08's and T12's completion criteria observable without interpreting intent — a named artifact, a named count, or a named absence? **Wrong shape**: "session restore works" — a model declares success on any non-crashing page. [Measurability, Plan T08 / T12]
- [x] CHK028 - Are verification steps specified per task such that each can be run and pass independently? **Wrong shape**: verification deferred to a final sweep, so a model marks five tasks done against one end-to-end run. [Measurability, Plan §tasks]
- [x] CHK029 - Is the constraint that `apps/web` has no test runner stated as affecting how every web requirement is validated? **Wrong shape**: unstated, so a model cites a clean `typecheck` as proof an auth requirement holds. [Dependency, Gap, Plan §Technical Context]

## Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK030 - Are the requirements defined for a valid cookie with a **revoked** server session, on both the middleware check and the first API call? **Wrong shape**: the guard is treated as sufficient and the stale-cookie path is left to emerge at runtime. [Coverage, Exception Flow, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK031 - Are the requirements defined for the cookie being present on the dashboard origin but the API being unreachable? **Wrong shape**: unstated — the guard passes on cookie presence while every data call fails, and the specified error states do not cover the combination. [Coverage, Exception Flow]
- [x] CHK032 - Are the requirements defined for mount-time restore racing against a user's first navigation? **Wrong shape**: unstated, so restore resolves after the first data call and overwrites state mid-render. [Coverage, Concurrency]
- [x] CHK033 - Are the requirements defined for logout while a mount-time restore is still in flight? **Wrong shape**: unstated — the restore resolves after logout and re-establishes a session the user just ended. [Coverage, Concurrency]
- [x] CHK034 - Is the recovery requirement for a reused or expired reset token specified with the exact failure the user sees? **Wrong shape**: a generic error, leaving a user who followed an old email with no path forward. [Coverage, Recovery Flow, Spec §FR-024]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK035 - Is the assumption that the backend cookie, CORS, and e2e coverage are already implemented validated with a reference to the commit or files, rather than asserted? **Wrong shape**: asserted — the plan's earlier version listed shipped work as pending and would have caused a rebuild. [Assumption, Plan §Scope reality check]
- [x] CHK036 - Is the mobile client's continued reliance on body-based refresh stated as a constraint the cookie change must not break? **Wrong shape**: unstated, so a model removes the body fallback as dead code for the web client. [Assumption, Spec §FR-016]
- [x] CHK037 - Is the assumption that the `@alfahd/types` dependency is required for correctness — not only tidiness — stated, given the dashboard's own types contradict the wire format? **Wrong shape**: treated as a style preference and skipped, leaving `success` and `CUSTOMER_SERVICE` in place. [Assumption, Plan T07 / Constitution §I]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [x] CHK038 - Is the conflict between FR-008 (guard reads the cookie) and cookie path scoping resolved in one place, so a reader cannot satisfy one and violate the other? **Wrong shape**: both requirements stand unqualified and are individually reasonable. [Conflict, Spec §FR-008 / FR-016]
- [x] CHK039 - Is the term "session" defined once, distinguishing the Redis server session, the browser cookie, and the in-memory access token? **Wrong shape**: undefined — an implementer clears the wrong one when clearing state. [Ambiguity, Spec §Key Entities]
- [x] CHK040 - Is the requirement for cookie clear-on-logout stated to use the identical `Path` used at set time? **Wrong shape**: unstated, so logout appears to succeed while the browser retains the cookie. [Ambiguity, Plan T01 / T14]
- [x] CHK041 - Is the redirect target after login specified for the case where the `redirect` parameter is absent, present, and present-but-external? **Wrong shape**: unstated for the external case, allowing an open-redirect requirement to go unspecified. [Ambiguity, Gap, Spec §FR-001]
- [x] CHK042 - Is the requirement for the login error message specified as identical regardless of status code, so a model cannot add a helpful-but-distinct 429 or 403 branch that leaks account state? **Wrong shape**: per-status messaging permitted generally, with only 401 constrained. [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-022 / FR-011]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
- **Highest-value items**: CHK003, CHK006, CHK007, CHK026 (T08 cookie name and T12 user-object fork — the two decisions a cheap model will otherwise invent), then CHK001/CHK038 (cookie `Path`, where the wrong value silently breaks auth)
